GomeBoy 1.3.0 fixes a network link-cable hang: an external-clock peer that is
slow or still negotiating no longer starves the HALT scheduler, so frames and
other events keep making progress.

The emulator still only implements serial hardware. Game-specific trading or
battle logic stays in the peer that implements `pkg/link`.

## Network link cable

When the remote endpoint supplies the clock, GomeBoy polls queued pulses on the
emulator scheduler thread. A non-ready poll used to reschedule every 32 ticks.
With the CPU halted that monopolized `skipHALT`, so a silent or mid-handshake
peer (for example a PokéPilot virtual trade) could hang the run.

1.3.0 exponentially backs off unsuccessful external-clock polls from 32 ticks
up to 4096 ticks, then resets the delay as soon as a transfer starts or a pulse
becomes ready. The pending transfer is not cancelled, and no wall-clock
watchdog is involved. The poll delay is part of serial snapshots/restores.

See [docs/LINK_CABLE.md](https://github.com/maestroi/gomeboy/blob/v1.3.0/docs/LINK_CABLE.md).

## Other changes since 1.2.0

- Core-neutral emulator boundary for lifecycle, stepping, framebuffer, state, and checkpoints (prep for a future GBA core)
- 32-bit `Read8At` / `ReadAt` / `ReadIntoAt` / `Peek8At` / `PeekIntoAt` APIs and core-dependent `AddressSpaceSize()`
- Checkpoints are now opaque and core-owned; existing GB/GBC APIs remain

## Binaries

| Asset | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gomeboy-linux-amd64` | Desktop GLFW emulator |
| `gomeboy-stream-linux-amd64` | FFmpeg CLI for live RGB encoding and `.gbrun` replay-to-video |
| `gomeboy-link-broker-linux-amd64` | Multi-session TCP link-cable broker |
